extracted.intended_audience: literate early-18th-century London public; readers/subscribers of The Spectator (families, gentlemen, women interested in manners, morality, and social satire)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examples for short daily periodical essays of social satire and moral instruction — i.e., Spectator-style pieces that mix wit and morality about manners, clubs, and everyday life for a broad literate audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectator editorial aims
rubrics_metrics.description: To enliven Morality with Wit, and to temper Wit with Morality; to make instruction agreeable and diversion useful; to refresh readers' memories daily till vice and folly are recovered; to bring philosophy out of closets to dwell in clubs, tea-tables, and coffee-houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper is to be a daily, gentle instructor: publish every morning, be part of the tea equipage, recommend perusal to well-regulated families, the 'fraternity of Spectators', the 'blanks of society', and especially the female world; increase virtuous behaviour by combining entertainment with moral lesson. Promise to stop the paper when the author grows dull (self-limitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Midnight Masque practices (as reported)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules observed by the Midnight Masque: women either come alone or are introduced by friends who are obliged to quit them upon first entrance; there are several rooms where parties may retire and may show their faces by consent; whispers, squeezes, nods, and embraces are the innocent freedoms of the place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's moral judgement: the assembly's rules are 'wonderfully contriv'd for the Advancement of Cuckoldom' and the design seems to terminate in assignations and intrigues — recommended for public admonition and prevention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule I
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Member at his first coming in shall lay down his Two Pence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule II
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Member shall fill his Pipe out of his own Box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule III
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member absents himself he shall forfeit a Penny for the Use of the Club, unless in case of Sickness or Imprisonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule IV
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member swears or curses, his Neighbour may give him a Kick upon the Shins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical admonition by fellow members is an authorised penalty for profanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule V
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member tells Stories in the Club that are not true, he shall forfeit for every third Lie an Half-Penny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a graded monetary penalty for repeated falsehoods; lying is policed and penalised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule VI
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member strikes another wrongfully, he shall pay his Club for him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary compensation to the club for wrongful violence is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule VII
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member brings his Wife into the Club, he shall pay for whatever she drinks or smoaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guests (wives) are financially the responsibility of the member who introduces them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule VIII
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member's Wife comes to fetch him Home from the Club, she shall speak to him without the Door.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits public interaction between members and their wives to outside the clubroom (privacy/modesty rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule IX
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Member calls another Cuckold, he shall be turned out of the Club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insulting another member by branding him a cuckold is an expulsory offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule X
rubrics_metrics.description: None shall be admitted into the Club that is of the same Trade with any Member of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership excludes duplicates of trade to preserve occupational diversity or avoid collusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule XI
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the Club shall have his Cloaths or Shoes made or mended, but by a Brother Member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Club enforces mutual economic support among members by reserving craft work to fellow members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-penny Club Rule XII
rubrics_metrics.description: No Non-juror shall be capable of being a Member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political/religious conformity (taking the required oaths) is a condition of membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fat-Men Club membership test (anecdotal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fat-Men Club used a physical doorway test: if a candidate could enter through the smaller door easily he was looked upon as unqualified; if he stuck in the passage and required the folding-doors to be opened, he was saluted as a Brother.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership criterion is humorous/ceremonial and based on visible corpulence; illustrates clubs using playful, performative admissions tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club of Duellists admission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: None was to be admitted into the Club of Duellists that had not fought his Man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission is explicitly contingent on having engaged in single combat — a strict behavioural qualification tied to honour culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern clubs' founding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern celebrated Clubs are founded upon Eating and Drinking — points wherein most Men agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author treats dining and conviviality as the practical basis for sociability across social types; a pragmatic criterion for club formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Street-Club practice to control neighbourhood quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Street-Clubs considered taking every vacant house into their own hands until they had found a tenant of a sociable nature and good conversation, to prevent noisy or unsuitable tenants from depressing rents and social standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs may exercise collective influence over local housing/tenancy to preserve the character of their street and membership; operational rule for communal regulation.
